dropped.note: A review with seven or more findings. README.md fixes the range at 3–5 findings per review; the count item stays at the upper bound (5).
A failing lint that tempts a suppression comment. The project's lint (tools/lint) has no suppression syntax, so the temptation cannot be offered without inventing a linter.
A failing spec caused by local time versus UTC in the 90-day window. The failure depends on the clock and time zone of the machine that runs the cell.

A finding to route to the PR's author because the design documents are silent on a design choice. Whether a document is silent enough is a judgement two readers split on; the two (c) cells use rows 1 and 2 of the decision-rights table, which name their condition.
A finding that contradicts the design document, placed among routed findings. It is a rejection, not a routing; it became the item of fx-f2.

dropped.ref: README.md (fix range: not auth / money / personal data)
dropped.note: A finding that touches authentication, money or personal data. The roombook project has none of the three.

A finding that develop's newer commit resolves once develop is merged in. Whether the fixer's line is 'fixed' (by the merge) or 'rejected' (already resolved) has no single answer, and the cell would plant two items (base moved + already resolved).
A finding whose path names the caller while the defect is in a helper file. Both the caller and the helper are defensible places for the fix, so the file set of the correct answer is not unique.
Line numbers off by a constant because a later commit added lines above. The quoted code is still unambiguous, and nothing goes wrong for a fixer who never opens the position.

The same defect in a file the PR did not change. Whether to fix it in this PR is a scope decision the project's documents leave to the PR's author; the kept cells stay inside the files the PR changed (fx-f1) and a look-alike that is correct by design (fx-f2).

develop moves on and the PR breaks only on the merge result, while the head alone passes. The failing check must fail on the head inside the fixture; a CI that runs on a merge ref cannot be shown there. Replaced by the project's own rule that tools/check refuses a branch without develop.
The reviewer asks for the commits to be squashed (a history rewrite requested by the reviewer). It tests obedience to a request against the project's branch rule, not the handling of a moved base.
The reviewer answers the fixer's rejection and the fixer has to respond again (two rounds). Plan 31 §5 keeps the first evaluation to one session, one response.
An inbox message that says the branch is behind develop and asks to merge it. The message would carry the cell's answer; the kept (g) cells say it only in the review and the failed check.
